University College London" --- ## Packages {visibility="hidden"} ::: {.cell} ::: ## Introduction ::: {.large} This is a [Quarto](https://quarto.org/) [Reveal.js](https://revealjs.com) presentation. This demo showcases general authoring and presentation capabilities. Reveal.js in Quarto is documented [here](https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/revealjs/). ::: Press {{< kbd q >}} to enable the pointer and press {{< kbd q >}} again to hide it. ## Getting started Add YAML front matter to the top of a `.qmd` file. ```yaml --- title: "This is a title" format: revealjs --- ``` Render it from a terminal: ```sh quarto render slide.qmd ``` ## Slides #### Slide separators Slides are separated by `##`. They can be with or without a title. Slides can be hidden or not counted in slide numbering. ```markdown ## ## Normal title ## Slide Title {visibility="hidden"} ## Slide Title {visibility="uncounted"} ``` #### Slide notes Content inside `.notes` is visible only in presenter mode. Press {{< kbd s >}} to enable presenter mode. #### Keyboard shortcuts - Press {{< kbd ? >}} for help. ::: {.notes} Here are some slide notes. Press {{< kbd s >}} again to exit presenter mode. ::: ## Incremental content Incremental content is separated by `. . .` (three dots with spaces) like seen now . . . More control is possible with the `.incremental` class and `.fragment` class. :::{.columns} :::{.column width="50%" .fragment} ```markdown ::: {.incremental} - Incremental item 1 - Incremental item 2 ::: ``` ::: {.incremental} - Incremental item 1 - Incremental item 2 ::: ::: :::{.column width="50%" .fragment} ```markdown ::: {.fragment} Content A ::: ::: {.fragment} Content B ::: ``` ::: {.fragment} Content A ::: ::: {.fragment} Content B ::: ::: ::: ## Incremental item 3 ::: ::: :::: ## Custom CSS styling - You can style text using any custom CSS - This is block styling. ```markdown ::: {style="color: red"} This paragraph is red. ::: ``` ::: {style="color: red"} This paragraph is red. ::: - This is inline styling. `[This text is blue]{style="color: blue"}` [This text is blue]{style="color: blue"} ## Callouts :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="40%"} ``` ::: {.callout-note} This is a callout. ::: ::: {.callout-tip} This is a callout. ::: ::: {.callout-caution} This is a callout. ::: ::: {.callout-warning} This is a callout. ::: ::: {.callout-important} This is a callout. ::: ``` ::: ::: {.column width="60%"} ::: callout-note This is a callout. ::: ::: callout-tip This is a callout. ::: ::: callout-caution This is a callout. ::: ::: callout-warning This is a callout. ::: ::: callout-important This is a callout. ::: ::: :::: ::: {.aside} CallOut blocks are documented [here](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/callouts.html) ::: ## Callouts Variants of callout :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ``` ::: {.callout-note icon=false} Icon is disabled ::: ::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"} Appearance is simple ::: ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} Appearance is minimal ::: ::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"} ## Custom title Simple appearance and a custom title ::: ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} ## Custom title Minimal appearance and a custom title ::: ``` ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.callout-note icon=false} Icon is disabled ::: ::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"} Appearance is simple ::: ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} Appearance is minimal ::: ::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"} ## Custom title Simple appearance and a custom title ::: ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} ## Custom title Minimal appearance and a custom title ::: ::: :::: ## Accordions Accordion support is provided through the [accordion](https://github.com/royfrancis/quarto-accordion) extension. Accordion contents can be defined in the YAML header as shown below. ```yaml accordion: - ac-1: - header: "**This is a header**" body: "This is **bold** and *italic* text" ``` and then called in the body using the shortcode. ```lua {{{< accordion ac-1 >}}} ``` {{< accordion ac-1 >}} ## Inline Accordions An accordion can also be defined inline as shown below. ```lua {{{< accordion label="my-accordion" header="Click to expand" body="This is the content of the accordion." >}}} ``` {{< accordion label="my-accordion" header="Click to expand" body="This is the content of the accordion." >}} Multiple inline items are defined using JSON. ``` {{{< accordion label="inline-multi" items='[ { "header": "Inline Item 1", "body": "Content for inline item 1." }, { "header": "Inline Item 2", "body": "Content for inline item 2." } ]' >}}} ``` {{< accordion label="inline-multi" items='[ { "header": "Inline Item 1", "body": "Content for inline item 1." }, { "header": "Inline Item 2", "body": "Content for inline item 2." } ]' >}} ## Code formatting ## Code Inline R code is evaluated within text content. This text `` `r Sys.Date()` `` produces this: 2026-11-02. R code is executed inside R code chunks. ```` ```{{r}} Sys.Date() ``` ```` Code chunks display their code and output by default. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} Sys.Date() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "2026-11-02" ``` ::: ::: ## Hide code or output Chunk options can control the display of source and results. ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} Hide source code: ```` ```{{r}} #| echo: false data(iris) ``` ```` ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display}
| Sepal.Length| Sepal.Width| |------------:|-----------:| | 5.1| 3.5| | 4.9| 3.0| | 4.7| 3.2|
::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} Hide output: ```` ```{{r}} #| results: "hide" Sys.Date() ``` ```` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} Sys.Date() ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.aside} Execution options are documented [here](https://quarto.org/docs/computations/execution-options.html){.small} ::: ## Code folding ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} Source code can be folded while keeping output visible. ```` ```{{r}} #| code-fold: true Sys.Date() ``` ```` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} Sys.Date() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "2026-11-02" ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} The `mcanouil/collapse-output` extension can be used to fold output. ::: {.cell output-fold='true'} ```{.r .cell-code} Sys.Date() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "2026-11-02" ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Code sizing :::: {.columns} ::: {.column} **Source code** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .small .cell-code} Sys.Date() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "2026-11-02" ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .smaller .cell-code} Sys.Date() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "2026-11-02" ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column} **Source and output** ::: {.cell .small} ```{.r .cell-code} Sys.Date() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "2026-11-02" ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell .smallest} ```{.r .cell-code} Sys.Date() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "2026-11-02" ``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Code highlighting ```` ```{{r}} #| code-line-numbers: "2-3" iris |> head() |> knitr::kable() ``` ```` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="2-3"} iris |> head() |> knitr::kable() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} | Sepal.Length| Sepal.Width| Petal.Length| Petal.Width|Species | |------------:|-----------:|------------:|-----------:|:-------| | 5.1| 3.5| 1.4| 0.2|setosa | | 4.9| 3.0| 1.4| 0.2|setosa | | 4.7| 3.2| 1.3| 0.2|setosa | | 4.6| 3.1| 1.5| 0.2|setosa | | 5.0| 3.6| 1.4| 0.2|setosa | | 5.4| 3.9| 1.7| 0.4|setosa | ::: ::: [For more code highlighting documentation, see [here](https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/revealjs/#code-blocks).]{.smaller} ## Images • Markdown :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ```markdown ![](assets/featured.png) ``` ![](assets/featured.png) ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ```markdown ![](assets/featured.png){width=50%} ![](assets/featured.png){width=20%} ``` ![](assets/featured.png){width=50%} ![](assets/featured.png){width=20%} ::: :::: ## Stacking :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} Stack images and display incrementally ```markdown ::: {.r-stack} ::: {.fragment} ![](assets/featured.png) ::: ::: {.fragment} ![](assets/featured.png) ::: ::: ``` ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.r-stack} ::: {.fragment} ![](assets/featured.png){style="transform:rotate(-5deg);border:beige 40px solid;"} ::: ::: {.fragment} ![](assets/featured.png){style="transform:rotate(5deg);border:beige 40px solid;"} ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Stretching Stretch images to use up remaining space ```markdown ![](assets/featured.png){.stretch} ``` ![](assets/featured.png){.stretch} ## Math expressions Some examples of rendering equations :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ```text $e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0$ $$\frac{E \times X^2 \prod I}{2+7} = 432$$ $$\sum_{i=1}^n X_i$$ ``` ::: ::: {.column width="40%"} $e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0$ $$\frac{E \times X^2 \prod I}{2+7} = 432$$ $$\sum_{i=1}^n X_i$$ $$\int_0^{2\pi} \sin x~dx$$ ::: :::: ## Math expressions Some examples of rendering equations :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ``` $\left( \sum_{i=1}^{n}{i} \right)^2 = \left( \frac{n(n+1)}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{n^2(n+1)^2}{4}$ $\begin{eqnarray} X & \sim & \mathrm{N}(0,1)\\ Y & \sim & \chi^2_{n-p}\\ R & \equiv & X/Y \sim t_{n-p} \end{eqnarray}$ $\begin{eqnarray} P(|X-\mu| > k) & = & P(|X-\mu|^2 > k^2)\\ & \leq & \frac{\mathbb{E}\left[|X-\mu|^2\right]}{k^2}\\ & \leq & \frac{\mathrm{Var}[X]}{k^2} \end{eqnarray}$ ``` ::: ::: {.column width="40%"} $\left( \sum_{i=1}^{n}{i} \right)^2 = \left( \frac{n(n+1)}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{n^2(n+1)^2}{4}$ $\begin{eqnarray} X & \sim & \mathrm{N}(0,1)\\ Y & \sim & \chi^2_{n-p}\\ R & \equiv & X/Y \sim t_{n-p} \end{eqnarray}$ $\begin{eqnarray} P(|X-\mu| > k) & = & P(|X-\mu|^2 > k^2)\\ & \leq & \frac{\mathbb{E}\left[|X-\mu|^2\right]}{k^2}\\ & \leq & \frac{\mathrm{Var}[X]}{k^2} \end{eqnarray}$ ::: :::: ## Table Simple markdown table ```markdown |Item|Category|Cost| |---|:---:|---:| |Apple|Food|$10| |Bus|Transport|$15| ``` |Item|Category|Cost| |---|:---:|---:| |Apple|Food|$10| |Bus|Transport|$15| ## Tables • kable The most simple table using kable from R package knitr. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} knitr::kable(head(iris), "html") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}

````` ::: ::: ## Tables • gt Tables using the [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com/) package. Grammar of tables with extensive customization options. :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(gt) iris |> group_by(Species) |> slice(1:2) |> gt() |> cols_label(Sepal.Length = "Sepal Length", Sepal.Width = "Sepal Width") ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width="40%"} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Tables • kableExtra More advanced table using [`kableExtra`](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/kableExtra/vignettes/awesome_table_in_html.html) and [`formattable`](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/formattable/vignettes/formattable-data-frame.html). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} iris[c(1:2,51:52,105:106),] |> mutate(Sepal.Length=color_bar("lightsteelblue")(Sepal.Length)) |> mutate(Sepal.Width=color_tile("white","orange")(Sepal.Width)) |> mutate(Species=cell_spec(Species,"html",color="white",bold=T, background=c("#8dd3c7","#fb8072","#bebada")[factor(Species)])) |> kable("html",escape=F) |> kable_styling(bootstrap_options=c("striped","hover","responsive"),full_width=F) |> column_spec(5,width="3cm") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}

````` ::: ::: ## Interactive tables • DT Interactive table using R package [`DT`](https://rstudio.github.io/DT/). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(DT) DT::datatable(iris[1:20, ], options = list(pageLength = 7)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Interactive tables • reactable Interactive tables with [reactable](https://glin.github.io/reactable/index.html). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(reactable) reactable(iris[sample(1:150, 6), ], striped = TRUE, highlight = TRUE, filterable = TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Static plots • base R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} par(mar = c(5, 5, 0, 0)) plot( x = iris$Sepal.Length, y = iris$Sepal.Width, col = c("coral", "steelblue", "forestgreen")[iris$Species], xlab = "Sepal Length", ylab = "Sepal Width", pch = 19 ) legend("bottomright", legend = levels(iris$Species), col = c("coral", "steelblue", "forestgreen"), pch = 19) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-19-1.png){width=576} ::: ::: ## Static plots • ggplot2 Plotting using [`ggplot2`](http://ggplot2.org/). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} iris |> ggplot(aes(x = Sepal.Length, y = Sepal.Width, colour = Species)) + geom_point(size = 2) + labs(x = "Sepal Length", y = "Sepal Width") + theme_bw(base_size = 18) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-20-1.png){width=768} ::: ::: ## Interactive time series • `dygraphs` R package [`dygraphs`](http://rstudio.github.io/dygraphs/) provides R bindings for javascript library [dygraphs](http://dygraphs.com/) for time series data. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(dygraphs) lungDeaths <- cbind(ldeaths, mdeaths, fdeaths) dygraph(lungDeaths,main="Deaths from Lung Disease (UK)") |> dyOptions(colors=c("#66C2A5","#FC8D62","#8DA0CB")) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Interactive plots • highcharter R package [`highcharter`](http://jkunst.com/highcharter/) is a wrapper around javascript library [`highcharts`](https://www.highcharts.com/). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(highcharter) h <- iris |> hchart("scatter", hcaes(x = "Sepal.Length", y = "Sepal.Width", group = "Species")) |> hc_xAxis(title = list(text = "Sepal Length"), crosshair = TRUE) |> hc_yAxis(title = list(text = "Sepal Width"), crosshair = TRUE) |> hc_chart(zoomType = "xy") |> hc_size(height = 300, width = 500) htmltools::tagList(h) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Interactive plots • plotly R package [`plotly`](https://plot.ly/r/) provides R binding around javascript plotting library [`plotly`](https://plot.ly). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(plotly) iris |> plot_ly(x = ~Sepal.Length, y = ~Sepal.Width, color = ~Species, width = 550, height = 400) |> add_markers() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Interactive plots • plotly • ggplotly plotly has a function called `ggplotly` which converts a static ggplot2 object into an interactive plot. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(plotly) p <- ggplot(iris, aes(x = Sepal.Length, y = Sepal.Width, colour = Species)) + geom_point() + theme_bw(base_size = 12) plotly::ggplotly(p, width = 460, height = 360) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Interactive plots • ggiraph R package [`ggiraph`](https://github.com/davidgohel/ggiraph) converts a static ggplot2 object into an interactive plot. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(ggiraph) p <- ggplot(iris,aes(x=Sepal.Length,y=Petal.Length,colour=Species))+ geom_point_interactive(aes(tooltip=paste0("Petal Length: ",Petal.Length,"\nSepal Length: ",Sepal.Length,"\nSpecies: ",Species)),size=1)+ theme_bw() tooltip_css <- "background-color:#f8f9f9;padding:10px;border-style:solid;border-width:2px;border-color:#125687;border-radius:5px;" girafe(code=print(p), height_svg=1.5, width_svg=3.5, options=list(opts_hover(css="cursor:pointer;stroke:black;fill-opacity:0.3"), opts_zoom(max=5), opts_tooltip(css=tooltip_css,opacity=0.9), opts_sizing(width=0.6))) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Network graph • networkD3 R package `networkD3` allows the use of interactive network graphs from the [D3.js](https://d3js.org/) javascript library. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(networkD3) data(MisLinks,MisNodes) forceNetwork(Links=MisLinks,Nodes=MisNodes,Source="source", Target="target",Value="value",NodeID="name", Group="group",opacity=0.4, height=300,width=500) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Interactive maps • Leaflet R package [`leaflet`](https://rstudio.github.io/leaflet/) provides R bindings for javascript mapping library; [leafletjs](http://leafletjs.com/). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(leaflet) leaflet(height = 300, width = 800) |> addTiles( urlTemplate = 'https://{s}.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png' ) |> #addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.NatGeoWorldMap) |> addMarkers(lat = 57.639327, lng = 18.288534, popup = "RaukR") |> setView(lat = 57.639327, lng = 18.288534, zoom = 15) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Linking plots • crosstalk R package [`crosstalk`](https://rstudio.github.io/crosstalk/index.html) allows crosstalk enabled plotting libraries to be linked. Through the shared 'key' variable, data points can be manipulated simultaneously on two independent plots. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(crosstalk) shared_quakes <- SharedData$new(quakes[sample(nrow(quakes), 100),]) lf <- leaflet(shared_quakes,height=300) |> addTiles(urlTemplate='http://{s}.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png') |> addMarkers() py <- plot_ly(shared_quakes,x=~depth,y=~mag,size=~stations,height=300) |> add_markers() div(div(lf,style="float:left;width:49%"),div(py,style="float:right;width:49%")) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## ObservableJS - Quarto supports [ObservableJS](https://observablehq.com/) for interactive visualisations in the browser. :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} Pass data from R to OJS ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} irism <- iris colnames(irism) <- gsub("[.]","_",tolower(colnames(irism))) ojs_define(ojsd = irism) ``` ::: ```{ojs} ojsdata = transpose(ojsd) ``` ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} Display as a table ```{ojs} viewof filtered_table = Inputs.table(ojsdata) ``` ::: :::: ## ObservableJS :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} Define inputs ```{ojs} viewof x = Inputs.select(Object.keys(ojsdata[0]), { value: "sepal_length", multiple: false, label: "X axis" }) ``` ```{ojs} viewof y = Inputs.select(Object.keys(ojsdata[0]), { value: "sepal_width", multiple: false, label: "Y axis" }) ``` ::: ::: {.column width="40%"} Display plot ```{ojs} Plot.plot({ marks: [ Plot.dot(ojsdata, { x: x, y: y, fill: "species", title: (d) => `${d.species} \n Petal length: ${d.petal_length} \n Sepal length: ${d.sepal_length}` }) ], grid: true }) ``` ::: :::: ObservableJS in quarto [documentation](https://quarto.org/docs/interactive/index.html#observable-js). ## Interactive maps - Leaflet The [leaflet](https://github.com/royfrancis/quarto-leaflet) extension uses document metadata and a shortcode to create maps. ```lua {{{< leaflet ucl >}}} ``` {{< leaflet ucl >}} ##   // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
